name: mkldnn_adaptive_avg_pool2d_backward
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim: aten::mkldnn_adaptive_avg_pool2d_backward(Tensor grad_output, Tensor self) -> Tensor. This representative selection is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full contract for all registered overloads, including keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and must never be narrowed to this one signature. All supplied registered signatures, verbatim: aten::mkldnn_adaptive_avg_pool2d_backward.out(Tensor grad_output, Tensor self, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!) and aten::mkldnn_adaptive_avg_pool2d_backward(Tensor grad_output, Tensor self) -> Tensor. Semantics (derived from the pytest): it is the backward of oneDNN adaptive average pooling 2d; the average window is derived from shapes as kernel_size[k - 2] = self.size(k) // grad_output.size(k), and each grad_output value is spread uniformly over that window to produce the gradient w.r.t. self. Both operands are positional Tensors; the result is a Tensor in the same oneDNN (torch._mkldnn) host layout as the operands. Dispatch is MkldnnCPU only, so the operator requires opaque oneDNN operands. The companion .out overload takes the same two positional operands plus a required keyword-only out Tensor; it writes into that buffer, returns the very same buffer object, and reports out as a mutated parameter (the default overload mutates nothing and aliases no argument). Error behavior stays in pytest: non-4D operands, extents not divisible by the derived window, a zero grad_output extent, dense (non-MkldnnCPU) operands, a dense out buffer, unsupported dtypes, and the missing backward gradient for this operator. No default for any parameter is invented; this signature has no optional or keyword-only parameters.
